paper.title: Chemical staining for fundamental studies and optimization of binders in Li-ion battery negative electrodes

figures.topic: quantitative sensitivity in a model bilayer electrode
local binder morphologies and inferred CMC nanolayer thickness
binder surface coverage before and after calendering
initial CMC concentration, CBD agglomeration and electronic resistivity
phase inversion, binder gradients and pore ionic resistance

claims.claim: Ag and Br can be calibrated as markers for CMC and SBR in graphite electrodes
claims.boundary: cross-reactions and formulation-specific calibration remain necessary

claims.claim: three local binder morphology regimes can be separated by multi-voltage EsB
claims.boundary: the 10-15 nm thickness is model-inferred rather than a full-electrode direct measurement

claims.claim: calendering substantially reduces apparent CMC surface coverage
claims.boundary: direct electrochemical consequences were not tested in matched full cells

claims.claim: higher initial CMC concentration reduces large CBD agglomerates and electronic resistivity
claims.boundary: the proposed adsorption-saturation mechanism was not measured directly

claims.claim: acetone phase inversion changes binder distribution and lowers apparent pore ionic resistance
claims.boundary: full-cell performance, long-term stability and roll-to-roll scale-up remain unverified

claims.claim: the staining approach is incompatible with reactive nano-Si and LiFePO4 without further adaptation
claims.boundary: compatibility depends on particle surface chemistry and passivation
